title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Gospel not administered from a precise intention of damning anyone — damnation's desert arises from neglect and contempt God foresaw and would not hinder in the reprobate
pass_a_gloss: The Gospel therefore is not administered by God himself unto any man from a nearest and precise intention of damning him; but, his neglect and contempt intervening, there arises in the contemner the desert of damnation, which God foresaw would be, and was unwilling to hinder in all the reprobate.
pass_b_english: So God does not administer the Gospel to anyone from a nearest precise intention of damning him. When neglect and contempt intervene, desert of damnation arises in the despiser — which God foresaw and was unwilling to hinder in all the reprobate.
source_text: Evangelium igitur non administratur ab ipso Deo ulli homini ex proxima et precisa intentione illum damnandi; sed, interveniente ejus neglectu et contemptu, exoritur in contemnente meritum damnationis, quod Deus praevidebat fore, et nolebat impedire in omnibus reprobatis.
